question: Who stopped the lighthouse clock at Kessel, and why?

first_items: The keeper's rule risks the tower
ch1.line: Ines must restart the stopped clock, because the keeper's rule puts her father's tower at risk.
ch1.point: The stopped clock threatens the tower
ch1.key: Ines trusts Ada with the key
recap: Ines, the keeper's daughter, finds the lighthouse clock stopped, so the lamp does not turn and boats wait outside the bar. Under the keeper's rule, a keeper who breaks the clock's hour loses the tower.
Mr Hale, the harbour master, will not help, so Ines turns to Ada, a clockmaker who arrives on the evening boat. Because Ines cannot pay, she gives Ada her mother's compass and the key.

moments.name: The stopped clock
moments.text: The hands stand at ten minutes to six, so the lamp does not turn.

moments.name: Tomas says nothing
moments.text: Tomas, Ines's brother, looks at the floor when she says somebody stopped it.

moments.name: Mr Hale's warning
moments.text: The keeper will lose the tower unless the clock runs by Friday.

moments.name: The compass
moments.text: Ines pays Ada with her mother's brass compass, her only valuable thing.

moments.name: The key
moments.text: Ines gives Ada the key, the first person outside the family to hold it.

remember.title: The keeper's rule
remember.text: The lamp turns when the clock strikes the hour; a keeper who breaks it loses the tower.

remember.title: Ada
remember.text: A clockmaker from the city, come to repair the church clock.

questions.q: What is the keeper's rule in Kessel?
questions.a: The lamp turns when the clock strikes the hour, and a keeper who breaks it loses the tower.

questions.q: How does Ines pay Ada, and why?
questions.a: With her mother's brass compass, because she cannot pay Ada's price.

questions.q: What will Ines's father lose if the clock is not running by Friday?
questions.a: The tower and the house that goes with it.

ch2.before: The lighthouse clock at Kessel stopped, and under the keeper's rule Ines's father may lose the tower. Chapter 1: Ines paid Ada, a clockmaker, with her mother's compass and gave her the key.
ch2.line: Salt in the wheel shows somebody used a key, and Mr Hale borrowed one.
ch2.key: Ines keeps the key from Mr Hale
recap: Ada, the clockmaker, finds salt packed into the clock's main wheel, so somebody opened the case with a key. Only two keys exist, and Tomas, Ines's brother, admits he lent one to Mr Hale, the harbour master, for a silver coin.
Ada mends the clock, so the lamp turns and the boats come in. When Mr Hale asks for the key, Ines says her father will decide, and she hides it in the kitchen lamp.

moments.name: The salt
moments.text: Ada finds salt in the main wheel: it did not get there by chance.

moments.name: Two keys
moments.text: Only the keeper and Ines hold keys to the clock room.

moments.name: Tomas's coin
moments.text: Tomas lent the key to Mr Hale for a silver coin.

moments.name: The light returns
moments.text: At noon the clock strikes, so the lamp turns and the boats come in.

moments.name: The hidden key
moments.text: Ines will not give Mr Hale the key and hides it in the kitchen lamp.

remember.title: Mr Hale
remember.text: The harbour master; he borrowed the key and now wants it kept at his office.

remember.title: The salt
remember.text: Packed into the main wheel; Ada keeps it.

questions.q: Why did the lighthouse clock stop?
questions.a: Somebody packed salt into the teeth of its main wheel, after opening the case with a key.

questions.q: Who borrowed the key from Tomas?
questions.a: Mr Hale, the harbour master, for one evening, for a silver coin.

questions.q: Where does Ines hide the key?
questions.a: In the hollow base of the lamp in the kitchen.
